prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Select and listen to your pet's preferred desktop ambient soundscape while setup completes.", "Preview Desktop Habitat Ambience"]
1: ["Choose Your Desktop Companion", "Preview how your companion moves and lives on your desktop screen."]
2: ["Customize Pet Appearance & Accessories", "Select Companion Style"]
3: ["Watch how your pet will interact with your windows and taskbar when desktop setup finishes."]
4: ["Master Desktop Companion Controls", "Access your pet anytime from the system tray or use desktop shortcuts to hide and summon.", "Got It"]
5: ["Official Pet Adoption Certificate", "Name your companion and make your adoption pledge to finalize setup."]
6: ["Tip: Right-click your pet on desktop anytime to feed or play mini-games."]
7: ["Sign In to Protect Your Pet Data", "Your companion progress, items, and custom renders stay safe across devices.", "Continue with Account", "Automatic cloud backup prevents pet data loss."]
8: ["We will alert you with a gentle sound as soon as your pet lands on your desktop."]
9: ["Desktop Docking & Screen Controls", "Learn how your pet docks to screen borders and sits on top of open applications.", "Continue to Desktop"]
